subject: Tyska 4
title: Reading comprehension: an opinion text on the four-day work week
sourceSummary: A longer, argumentative German text about the debate over the shortened work week, with questions that require following the argument and drawing conclusions.

questions.prompt:
Read the text: "Die Vier-Tage-Woche wird seit einigen Jahren in vielen Ländern diskutiert, doch die Meinungen gehen weit auseinander. Befürworter argumentieren, dass kürzere Arbeitszeiten nicht nur die psychische Gesundheit der Angestellten verbessern, sondern auch die Produktivität steigern können – wer ausgeruht ist, arbeitet konzentrierter. Pilotprojekte in Island und Großbritannien scheinen diese These zu bestätigen: Die Umsätze der teilnehmenden Unternehmen blieben stabil, während die Mitarbeiterzufriedenheit deutlich zunahm. Kritiker hingegen warnen vor voreiligen Schlüssen. Sie weisen darauf hin, dass sich die Ergebnisse nicht ohne Weiteres auf alle Branchen übertragen lassen, besonders nicht auf das Gesundheitswesen oder die Industrie, wo schon jetzt Personalmangel herrscht. Außerdem befürchten manche Ökonomen, dass Unternehmen die eingesparte Zeit lediglich durch höheren Druck an den verbleibenden vier Tagen kompensieren würden – ein Ergebnis, das den ursprünglichen Zweck der Reform ins Gegenteil verkehren würde. Ob sich die Vier-Tage-Woche langfristig durchsetzt, bleibt daher, trotz vielversprechender erster Ergebnisse, eine offene Frage."

What is the text mainly about?
questions.opener: Look for the sentence that weighs both sides of the debate together.
choices: The history of how the four-day work week was invented
Whether the four-day work week is a good solution, with arguments both for and against
How an individual employee applies for shorter working hours
A description of one employee's daily life on a four-day schedule
questions.explanation: The text presents both the supporters' (Befürworter) and the critics' (Kritiker) arguments and ends by concluding that the question remains open. It's about the debate as a whole, not about history or one person's experience.

questions.prompt: Same text. Which argument do the supporters (Befürworter) use for the four-day work week?
questions.opener: The first half of the text presents their main argument in a single sentence.
choices: That it lowers companies' costs for office space
That it can improve mental health while also increasing productivity
That it is easy to introduce in every industry immediately
That it reduces the staff shortage in healthcare
questions.explanation: The text says the supporters believe shorter working hours "die psychische Gesundheit der Angestellten verbessern" and "die Produktivität steigern können" — that is, both better mental health and a possible productivity increase.

questions.prompt: Same text. What did the pilot projects in Iceland and the UK show, according to the text?
questions.opener: Look for the sentence with the words "Umsätze" and "Mitarbeiterzufriedenheit".
choices: Revenue dropped sharply while employee satisfaction decreased
Revenue stayed stable while employee satisfaction increased significantly
The companies were forced into bankruptcy within a year
The results were too uncertain to draw any conclusions at all
questions.explanation: "Die Umsätze der teilnehmenden Unternehmen blieben stabil, während die Mitarbeiterzufriedenheit deutlich zunahm" means that revenue was unchanged while employee satisfaction increased markedly.

questions.prompt: Same text. What is the critics' (Kritiker) main objection to generalizing the results?
questions.opener: The word "hingegen" marks where the text switches to the counter-arguments.
choices: That the results can't necessarily be transferred to every industry, especially not healthcare and manufacturing
That the pilot projects were never actually carried out
That the employees themselves didn't want to take part in the projects
That the four-day work week is already standard in most European countries
questions.explanation: The critics warn against "voreilige Schlüsse" (hasty conclusions) and argue that the results "sich nicht ohne Weiteres auf alle Branchen übertragen lassen", especially not to healthcare and manufacturing, where a staff shortage already exists.

questions.prompt: Same text. What are some economists worried about, according to the text?
questions.opener: The last argument in the text is about what companies might do with the "saved" time.
choices: That companies would compensate for the shorter week by raising everyone's pay
That companies would compensate for the saved time with increased pressure over the remaining four days, undermining the reform's purpose
That the government would ban the four-day work week entirely
That productivity would stay exactly the same as before
questions.explanation: The text says the economists fear companies would compensate for the time savings "durch höheren Druck an den verbleibenden vier Tagen" — a result that would turn the reform's original purpose into its opposite.

questions.prompt: Same text. What conclusion does the text ultimately draw about the future of the four-day work week?
questions.opener: Read the very last sentence carefully — what does it say, despite the positive results?
choices: That it will definitely be introduced everywhere within a few years
That it has already failed completely and been abandoned
That the question of long-term success remains open, despite promising early results
That only Iceland will continue using the model
questions.explanation: The last sentence says it "trotz vielversprechender erster Ergebnisse, eine offene Frage" (bleibt) — that is, the question remains unanswered despite promising initial results. The text does not take a definitive stance either way.

questions.prompt: Same text. Explain step by step the logic behind the economists' concern: why could more pressure over four days "den ursprünglichen Zweck der Reform ins Gegenteil verkehren" (turn the reform's original purpose into its opposite)?
questions.opener: Start with what the reform is actually supposed to achieve, then follow what happens if companies respond in a certain way.
questions.answer: If companies push staff harder over the remaining four days to make up for the lost working time, exactly the health benefit the reform was meant to provide disappears — the stress doesn't decrease, it just gets concentrated into fewer days.
steps: The reform's purpose, according to its supporters, is to improve employees' mental health and wellbeing through a shorter work week.
The economists' concern is that companies, in order to maintain the same output, increase the pace and pressure over the remaining four days.
If that happens, the health benefit disappears: total stress doesn't decrease, it just gets concentrated into fewer days instead of actually decreasing.
The result is the opposite of what the reform was meant to achieve — hence the phrase "ins Gegenteil verkehren" (to turn into its opposite).

questions.prompt: What strategies help you understand an argumentative, opinion-based German text like the one about the four-day work week?
questions.opener: Look for who is saying what, and which words mark a turn in the argument.
questions.answer: Identify the two sides early: who are the Befürworter (supporters) and who are the Kritiker (critics)? Look for signal words that mark a turn in the argument: hingegen/jedoch/allerdings (however/though), außerdem (in addition), daher (therefore). Pay attention to Konjunktiv II (würde kompensieren, würde verkehren) — it often marks an assumption or a feared consequence, not an established fact. Distinguish between facts the text reports (the pilot projects' results) and opinions/concerns different groups express. A text that ends with "bleibt eine offene Frage" rarely takes a definitive stance — summarize both sides rather than picking one.

questions.prompt:
Read the text: "Der Fleischkonsum in Deutschland ist in den letzten zehn Jahren spürbar zurückgegangen, doch er bleibt im europäischen Vergleich weiterhin hoch. Befürworter einer pflanzlichen Ernährung argumentieren vor allem mit dem Klimaschutz: Die Produktion von Fleisch, insbesondere von Rindfleisch, verursacht deutlich mehr Treibhausgase als der Anbau von Gemüse oder Hülsenfrüchten. Auch der hohe Wasser- und Flächenverbrauch der Tierhaltung wird häufig als Argument angeführt. Vertreter der Landwirtschaft weisen hingegen darauf hin, dass viele Weideflächen in Deutschland für den Anbau von Getreide oder Gemüse gar nicht geeignet wären, sodass die Tierhaltung dort tatsächlich die einzige sinnvolle Nutzung der Flächen darstelle. Zudem betonen sie die wirtschaftliche Bedeutung der Landwirtschaft für ländliche Regionen, wo viele Arbeitsplätze direkt oder indirekt von der Fleischproduktion abhängen. Ernährungswissenschaftler wiederum weisen darauf hin, dass ein moderater Fleischkonsum gesundheitlich unproblematisch sei, ein sehr hoher Konsum jedoch mit einem erhöhten Risiko für Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen in Verbindung gebracht werde. Eine einfache Antwort auf die Frage, wie viel Fleisch \"richtig\" ist, gibt es also nicht — die Debatte bewegt sich zwischen ökologischen, wirtschaftlichen und gesundheitlichen Argumenten."

What is the text mainly about?
questions.opener: Look for the different groups mentioned and their respective arguments.
choices: The debate about meat consumption in Germany, with arguments from several different perspectives
Instructions on how to become a vegetarian
A history of the development of German agriculture
A cookbook with meat-free recipes
questions.explanation: The text presents arguments from supporters of plant-based eating, agricultural representatives, and nutrition scientists — a multi-sided debate about meat consumption, not instructions, history, or a cookbook.

questions.prompt: Same text. Which argument do the supporters of pflanzliche Ernährung (plant-based eating) use?
questions.opener: The first half of the text mentions their main argument.
choices: Climate protection, since meat production causes more greenhouse gases
That meat tastes worse than vegetables
That it's cheaper to eat meat
That livestock farming requires less water
questions.explanation: The text says meat production "verursacht deutlich mehr Treibhausgase als der Anbau von Gemüse" (causes significantly more greenhouse gases than growing vegetables) — a climate argument.

questions.prompt: Same text. What does "die Weideflächen" mean in the context of the farmers' counter-argument?
questions.opener: The word comes from "weiden" (to graze) and "die Fläche" (area/land).
choices: Grazing land/pastures
Cropland for grain
Forest land
Industrial areas
questions.explanation: "Die Weideflächen" means grazing land/pastures, land where animals graze.

questions.prompt: Same text. What is the agricultural representatives' main argument against abolishing livestock farming entirely?
questions.opener: Look for the sentence about "Weideflächen" and "wirtschaftliche Bedeutung".
choices: Many pastures aren't suitable for other farming, and livestock farming provides important jobs
Meat is the only source of protein
Climate change isn't real
Consumers refuse to eat vegetables
questions.explanation: The text says many pastures aren't suitable for growing grain or vegetables, and that livestock farming has significant economic importance for rural areas.

questions.prompt: Same text. What can be inferred about the nutrition scientists' (Ernährungswissenschaftler) stance, based on the text?
questions.opener: Look for the sentence about "moderater Fleischkonsum" compared to "sehr hoher Konsum".
choices: They take a middle position: moderate meat consumption isn't a health risk, but very high amounts are
They believe all meat consumption is dangerous
They believe meat is completely risk-free regardless of amount
They have no opinion on the health question
questions.explanation: The text says moderate meat consumption is "gesundheitlich unproblematisch", while very high consumption is linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease — a nuanced middle position.

choices: Cardiovascular disease
Digestive problems
Allergies
Sleep problems

questions.prompt: Same text. What conclusion does the text draw about the question of how much meat is the "right" amount?
choices: There is no simple answer — the debate moves between ecological, economic, and health-related arguments
Experts fully agree on exactly how much meat one should eat
Meat should be banned entirely within a few years
The question is unimportant and rarely discussed
questions.explanation: The last sentence says there is no simple answer, and that the debate moves between ecological, economic, and health-related arguments.
